skill.name: sragent
skill.description: Query SRA and GEO datasets with SRAgent, convert genomics accessions, review metadata, retrieve linked publications, and identify single-cell sequencing technologies.
skill.summary: Use SRAgent to analyze public genomics datasets and linked publications.
skill.author: ArcInstitute

security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from Markdown examples, public database URLs, and expected Claude skill installation paths. Confirmed risks are unsafe secret-handling guidance that can print API keys, expose .env files, or pass keys through command arguments. No prompt injection text was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting commands can expose API keys and .env contents.
remediation.suggestion: Replace echo, env grep, and cat .env examples with masked presence checks such as ${VAR:+SET}.

remediation.issue: The setup flow asks users to provide missing environment variables.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to set secrets locally through their shell, credential manager, or platform secret store.

remediation.issue: One command passes CORE_API_KEY as a CLI argument.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer environment-based configuration or a local config file with clear masking guidance.

remediation.issue: Network and file writes are central to the workflow.
remediation.suggestion: Document that SRAgent contacts public databases and writes CSV or paper files to user-selected directories.

content.value_statement: Genomics researchers need fast ways to connect SRA, GEO, and publication records. This skill guides SRAgent workflows for accession conversion, metadata review, paper retrieval, and single-cell technology checks.
actual_capabilities: Converts GEO, SRA, BioProject, and ENA accessions across study, experiment, and run levels.
Runs SRAgent entrez, sragent, and papers workflows for dataset questions.
Extracts metadata such as organism, platform, library layout, and library preparation technology.
Identifies common single-cell and spatial transcriptomics technologies from public metadata.
Finds linked publications and records download status for open-access manuscripts.
Supports CSV-based batch processing and enrichment with publication identifiers.
limitations: Requires a local SRAgent installation and Python 3.11 or newer.
Needs valid provider keys for LLM features and optional keys for NCBI, CORE, and BigQuery.
Paper downloads depend on open-access availability and external source reliability.
Results should be checked against source databases for publication-quality analyses.

use_cases.title: Convert Dataset Accessions
use_cases.description: Convert GSE or BioProject identifiers into SRX and SRR accessions before downstream analysis.

use_cases.title: Audit Sequencing Metadata
use_cases.description: Check organism, platform, library layout, and single-cell status across public experiments.

use_cases.title: Collect Linked Papers
use_cases.description: Find publications connected to SRA accessions and summarize which manuscripts are available.

prompt_templates.title: Convert One Accession
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert GSE121737 into SRX experiment accessions and explain the result.

prompt_templates.title: Check Experiment Metadata
prompt_templates.prompt: Tell me the organism, sequencing platform, library layout, and single-cell status for SRX4967527.

prompt_templates.title: Find Dataset Papers
prompt_templates.prompt: Find publications linked to PRJNA498286 and summarize which papers can be retrieved.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Study Technologies
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare the single-cell technologies used in PRJNA498286 and PRJNA615032, then list evidence for each call.

output_examples.output: The response lists the matching SRX experiments, explains the GEO to SRA relationship, and notes any missing records.
The response states the single-cell decision, supporting library preparation evidence, organism, platform, and confidence caveats.

output_examples.input: Download papers for a CSV of accessions.
output_examples.output: The response summarizes processed accessions, linked publications, successful downloads, failed downloads, and output locations.

best_practices: Use exact accession identifiers and specify the output format you need.
Mask API keys and check only whether required environment variables are set.
Verify important metadata against NCBI, GEO, or publication records before citing results.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys or service credentials into chat prompts.
Do not assume every SRA dataset has a linked open-access manuscript.
Do not treat automated technology labels as final without checking supporting metadata.

faq.question: What databases does this skill help query?
faq.answer: It helps use SRAgent with SRA, GEO, ENA-style accessions, PubMed links, CORE, Europe PMC, and BigQuery metadata.

faq.question: Does it install SRAgent automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup and usage guidance. The user must install SRAgent and configure credentials locally.

faq.question: Can it identify single-cell sequencing technologies?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides checks for 10X Genomics, Smart-seq, Drop-seq, spatial methods, and related metadata signals.

faq.question: Can it download paywalled papers?
faq.answer: No. It can help locate linked publications, but downloads depend on open-access availability and source permissions.

faq.question: Which credentials may be needed?
faq.answer: LLM provider keys are required for SRAAgent features. NCBI, CORE, and Google Cloud credentials are optional for specific workflows.

faq.question: Is this a replacement for manual curation?
faq.answer: No. It speeds up discovery and metadata review, but final scientific claims need source verification.
